title: 10 Days in Italy
subtitle: Florence, Venice & Rome
summary: Ten days over Easter in Italy: five nights in Florence with day trips to Pisa, Lucca and Rome, then three nights in Venice with the islands and the Prosecco Hills. We filled it with Renaissance art, canals, ancient ruins and a lot of great pasta.

glance.label: Bases
glance.value: Florence (5 nights), Venice (3 nights), Florence (1 night)

glance.label: Getting around
glance.value: Frecciarossa high-speed and regional trains, vaporetto, FlixBus

intro: We built this trip around three of Italy's most storied cities, with day trips worked in. Five nights in Florence gave us time to breathe: the Uffizi, the Duomo, a day trip to Rome, a morning in Pisa and an afternoon cycling around Lucca. Three nights in Venice added the islands of Murano and Burano, a full day in the Prosecco Hills, and evenings spent getting lost in the calli on purpose. A final night back in Florence made for an easy departure.

We paced it on purpose: tours and sights in the morning, loose afternoons, and dinner reservations to look forward to after a long day. We pre-booked almost every big museum ticket, train and tour, and we noted where the timing had to be exact and where we could relax.

days_plan.label: Day 1
days_plan.title: Landing in Florence & a first aperitivo
days_plan.text: We fly out of Newark on Thursday afternoon and land in Florence on Friday with plenty of daylight left. We drop our bags, freshen up and head out. Tonight is for easing in, because tomorrow's 8:30 AM walking tour is one of the biggest mornings of the trip.

items.text: Overnight flight from Newark to Florence (leaving Thu, Apr 2)
Check in at Hotel L'Orologio Firenze on Piazza Santa Maria Novella, perfectly placed for exploring the center on foot

Wander Piazza Santa Maria Novella and the streets around it, then our first Italian aperitivo: a Negroni or Aperol Spritz at a café with outdoor seating. Mercato Centrale is close by if we'd rather graze
Dinner at L'Osteria di Giovanni, a classic Florentine trattoria

days_plan.tip: Don't overdo the first night: the Uffizi tour starts at 8:30 AM sharp.

days_plan.label: Day 2
days_plan.title: The Uffizi, the Duomo & the bell tower
days_plan.text: Our biggest day in Florence. We do a small-group Renaissance tour in the morning, climb Giotto's Campanile on a timed ticket after lunch, then visit Santa Croce, walk the shopping streets and catch sunset over the city.

items.text: Breakfast at the hotel and out the door by 8
Meet at the Florence & Global Tour office (Via Guelfa 12R) for the 4-hour small-group Uffizi and Accademia tour with 8:30 AM timed entry and a Duomo walk (Viator)

Cappuccino and a light lunch near the Arno, then the Ponte Vecchio, the only Florentine bridge not destroyed in WWII, and Piazza della Signoria, an open-air sculpture gallery with the Neptune Fountain and a replica of Michelangelo's David
Take in Santa Maria del Fiore (the Duomo) and the sheer scale of Brunelleschi's dome from Piazza del Duomo
Climb Giotto's Campanile for sweeping views over the whole city. We need to be in line by 2:05 and back down by 3:00
Rest, or grab a sandwich at Il Bufalo Trippone or Pino's Sandwiches / Salumeria Verdi
Basilica of Santa Croce with an audio tour. Michelangelo and Galileo are buried here
Museo dell'Opera del Duomo (included with the bell tower ticket, open until 7 PM), if we still have the energy
Gelato and the shopping streets: Via del Corso, Via dei Calzaiuoli, Via Roma to Piazza della Repubblica's carousel and cafés, and the luxury shops of Via de' Tornabuoni
Sunset at Piazzale Michelangelo or the quieter San Miniato al Monte just above it. The sun sets around 7:45
Dinner at Osteria Lucignolo, booked through TheFork with 30% off food

days_plan.tip: Timed entry at the Campanile is strict. Be in line by 2:05 PM and leave backpacks and large bags at the hotel.

days_plan.label: Day 3
days_plan.title: Easter: the Explosion of the Cart, Pitti Palace & a pasta class
days_plan.text: Easter Sunday in Florence. We start with the Scoppio del Carro outside the Duomo, which happens only once a year. Then we cross the river for the Bardini Gardens and Palazzo Pitti and spend the afternoon making pasta and gelato from scratch.

items.text: A slow, full breakfast at the hotel, since there's no proper meal until the cooking class

Scoppio del Carro in Piazza del Duomo. In this tradition dating to the 14th century, a cart loaded with fireworks is lit by a dove-shaped rocket during Easter mass for good fortune. It starts around 10–11 AM; arrive early for the crowds
Free time to pick and choose. Palazzo Pitti can be entered before the timed tour slot
Bardini Gardens: the baroque staircase, wisteria tunnel, panoramic terraces and fountains
30-minute guided tour of the Royal Apartments at Palazzo Pitti
Boboli Gardens (free entry today) if the lines are reasonable, or the Oltrarno's artisan workshops and leather shops
20-minute walk to the cooking school
Small-group pasta and gelato cooking class with Towns of Italy (Via Panicale). We eat what we make, finishing around 6 PM
Sunset at whichever viewpoint we missed yesterday
A light dinner: drinks over the Ponte Vecchio at the Hotel La Scaletta rooftop bar if it's open, or walk-in pizza at Mister Pizza or LiVio Pizzeria

days_plan.tip: Once you leave any museum in the Pitti complex you can't re-enter. Some Oltrarno shops may be closed on Easter Sunday.

days_plan.label: Day 4
days_plan.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa & cycling Lucca
days_plan.text: An early regional train to Pisa for the Piazza dei Miracoli and a climb up the Leaning Tower, then on to Lucca for an afternoon of cycling the Renaissance walls with food and wine tastings. We're back in Florence for a late cheese-wheel pasta dinner.

items.text: Coffee and a croissant to go from the hotel. Small bags only today
Regional train from Florence SMN to Pisa Centrale, arriving 8:42
Walk to the Piazza dei Miracoli, home to the Cathedral, Baptistery, Leaning Tower and Camposanto
A quick visit to the Baptistery of St. John (included with the Pisa ticket)
Climb the Leaning Tower on a timed slot (arrive by 9:30; bags may need to go in the cloakroom), plus the cathedral's marble floors and bronze doors and the frescoed Camposanto on the same ticket
Coffee and pastry at Pasticceria Salza near the square, then back to Pisa Centrale
Short regional train from Pisa to Lucca (tickets at the station or in the app)
A light lunch near the station: In Pasta – Cibo e Convivio, Fiaschetto or Ciacco on Piazza Napoleone

Lucca Bikes & Bites small-group tour (Viator) from the Tourist Center Lucca bike rental. We cycle the tree-lined Renaissance walls and the medieval streets with food and wine tastings along the way, until about 5:15
Train from Lucca back to Florence, arriving around 6:30
Dinner at Osteria Pastella, 5 minutes from the hotel, where the chef finishes our pasta in a cheese wheel at the table

days_plan.tip: Keep lunch in Lucca light, because the bike tour includes tastings. Osteria Pastella charges €20 if you cancel less than 2 hours ahead.

days_plan.label: Day 5
days_plan.title: Rome in a day: Colosseum, Pantheon & the Vatican
days_plan.text: A full day trip to Rome on the high-speed train. We tour the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine Hill in the morning, see the Pantheon after lunch and the Vatican Museums in the late afternoon, and finish with the Spanish Steps and Trevi Fountain before the late train home.

items.text: Leave the hotel for Firenze SMN
Frecciarossa 9591 from Florence to Roma Termini, a 90-minute ride arriving 8:35
Cappuccino and cornetto at Pasticceria Sessa 1930 by Termini, then the walk to the Colosseum
Guided tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill with The Tour Guide (be there by 9:30; it runs until about 1 PM)
Lunch: sit down at Pasqualino Al Colosseo dal 1956 (reserved online), or grab a quick sandwich at Mizio's Street Food, Sto Bene Roma or All'Antico Vinaio
Walk Via dei Fori Imperiali toward Piazza Venezia, past the Forum ruins
The Pantheon, one of Rome's most impressive ancient interiors
Taxi to the Vatican, booked in the Free Now app

Vatican Museums guided tour: check-in at 4, tour at 4:30, covering the Sistine Chapel, the Raphael Rooms and the vast collection. Afterward we walk Via dei Coronari or take a taxi to the Spanish Steps
The Spanish Steps and Piazza di Spagna in the evening light
Trevi Fountain with ground-level access tickets, then gelato at Gelato in Trevi
Walk or taxi to Roma Termini, arriving by 8:45
Frecciarossa 9568 back to Florence, arriving 10:58 PM. We sleep on the train

days_plan.tip: Eat a real lunch. We're inside the Vatican for hours after 4 PM, and there's little time for dinner before the train.

days_plan.label: Day 6
days_plan.title: Florence to Venice & a first evening on the canals
days_plan.text: A slow morning, then the high-speed train to Venice. We spend the afternoon wandering with no plan and end the night in St. Mark's Square, lit up after dark.

items.text: A slow breakfast at the hotel
Check out of Hotel L'Orologio and walk 10 minutes to Firenze SMN
Frecciarossa 9414 from Florence to Venezia Santa Lucia, arriving 1:34 PM
Walk or take a water taxi from the station and check in at Palazzo Veneziano
Our first stroll: get pleasantly lost in the calli, stop for cicchetti and an early aperitivo at a bacaro, then walk to the Rialto Bridge and along the Grand Canal
Dinner at Impronta Restaurant Venice, 15 minutes from the hotel
An evening walk through Piazza San Marco, lit at night, before tomorrow's crowds

days_plan.label: Day 7
days_plan.title: St. Mark's, the Doge's Palace & the islands
days_plan.text: A morning inside St. Mark's Basilica and the Doge's Palace, then the vaporetto out to Murano for glass-blowing and Burano for its colorful houses and lace.

items.text: Breakfast at the hotel, leaving by 8:50 for the 20-minute walk to the tour

Walks of Italy "Legendary Venice" tour of St. Mark's Basilica (including the terraces) and the full Doge's Palace, 9:30–12:30. We meet at the Correr Museum, Piazza San Marco 52, under the portico; look for the green Walks sign
Lunch nearby or on the islands, then the vaporetto to Murano and Burano
Dinner at San Silvestro Restaurant

days_plan.tip: Take vaporetto Line 4.1 or 4.2 from Fondamente Nove to Murano, then continue to Burano. Budget 3–4 hours for both islands, including at least 90 minutes on Burano.

days_plan.label: Day 8
days_plan.title: A full day in the Prosecco Hills
days_plan.text: A full-day vineyard tour in the UNESCO-listed Conegliano Valdobbiadene region, with rolling hills, historic estates and tastings of Prosecco where it was born.

items.text: Walk to Venezia Santa Lucia. The tour company provides the train tickets to the meeting point (Viator)
Prosecco Hills UNESCO tour through the Conegliano Valdobbiadene wine region
Train back to Venice (tickets provided by the tour), arriving around 6 PM
Dinner at a restaurant near the hotel

days_plan.tip: Reserve dinner before the day starts. You'll be tired and hungry when you get back and won't want to search.

days_plan.label: Day 9
days_plan.title: Venice to Florence & a final night
days_plan.text: We take the FlixBus from the mainland back to Florence for one last night at the Grand Hotel Cavour and a final dinner of our own choosing.

items.text: Breakfast at the hotel
Check out of Palazzo Veneziano and head to Venice Mestre: vaporetto or walk to Piazzale Roma, then a local train or bus across the causeway. We pick up drinks and snacks for the ride
FlixBus Route 466 from Venice Mestre (Stazione FS) to Florence Villa Costanza, arriving 3:40 PM
Taxi or tram from Villa Costanza and check in at the Grand Hotel Cavour for one night
Final dinner in Florence. It's our last free evening, and most of the center is walkable from the hotel

days_plan.tip: Venice Mestre is on the mainland, not in the historic center. Confirm your route there the night before.

days_plan.label: Day 10
days_plan.title: Arrivederci, Italia
days_plan.text: A very early start for a 7 AM flight home from Florence. Ten days done.

items.text: Very early ride to Florence Airport
Fly home from Florence, checking our bags at the counter

days_plan.tip: Pack the night before, leave everything by the door and set multiple alarms. Check your bags, since they'll likely be overweight after ten days of shopping and souvenirs.

tips.title: Keep tickets on your phone
tips.text: Our train tickets were in Google Wallet and our tour tickets in Apple Wallet. Check each ticket for its check-in instructions, review them before every departure, and screenshot everything before you leave home. Bring passports, since you'll need them for all travel.

tips.title: Respect the timed entries
tips.text: Some slots are strict and some are flexible, so know which is which. Be in line at Giotto's Campanile by 2:05 PM for a 2:15 slot, check in at the Vatican at 4 PM sharp, show your Palazzo Pitti ticket before 1 PM for priority access, and arrive at the cooking class by 2:45 PM for a 3 PM start.

tips.title: Pack layers and good shoes
tips.text: April in Italy is mild but variable. Comfortable shoes are non-negotiable on the cobblestones, and you'll want a light jacket for Venice evenings.

tips.title: Travel light on climb and bike days
tips.text: No big bags are allowed on the Campanile climb, and the Lucca bike tour calls for a small day bag. Leave everything else at the hotel.

tips.title: Catch the sunset
tips.text: In early April the sun sets around 7:45 PM in Florence. Be at the viewpoint by 7. With two evenings, try both Piazzale Michelangelo and San Miniato al Monte. San Miniato is quieter and better for photos on a clear night.

tips.title: Taxis and money
tips.text: Download the Free Now app for taxis in Rome. Uber works in some Italian cities. Cards are accepted almost everywhere, but small cash is handy for cafés and markets.

tips.title: Eat like a local
tips.text: Aperitivo hour runs roughly 6–8 PM, so don't miss it. In Venice, cicchetti are snacks at a bacaro (wine bar). Coffee means espresso, and it's cheaper standing at the bar. Many restaurant kitchens don't open until 7:30 PM or later, and gelato is the perfect follow-up to a sandwich lunch.

tips.title: Mind the fine print
tips.text: Check cancellation policies (Osteria Pastella charges €20 if you cancel within 2 hours) and check hotel breakfast hours before a late night.

tips.title: Learn a few words of Italian
tips.text: Locals appreciate the effort. Buongiorno (good morning), buonasera (good evening), per favore (please), grazie (thank you), un tavolo per due (a table for two), il conto, per favore (the check, please) and cin cin! (cheers) go a long way.
